question: Which hormone relaxes the muscles of the urinary tract during pregnancy, causing the ureters to widen?
explanation: Progesterone relaxes smooth muscles all over the body. During pregnancy, this causes the tubes carrying urine from the kidneys to widen. You've got this! [learn more](GNS121_U7_T5#GNS121_U7_T5_h1)

question: Why is swelling of the kidney drainage system (hydronephrosis) more common on the right side during pregnancy?

options.A: The right renal artery has a higher pressure than the left.
options.B: The pregnant uterus tilts and compresses the right ureter more.
options.C: The right kidney is anatomically larger than the left kidney.
options.D: Progesterone receptors are concentrated only in the right ureter.

explanation: The growing uterus tends to lean to the right, putting extra pressure on the right ureter. Small details like this make you a sharp clinical nurse! [learn more](GNS121_U7_T5#GNS121_U7_T5_h1)

question: What usually happens to the rate at which the kidneys filter blood (GFR) during a normal pregnancy?

options.A: It increases by about fifty percent.
options.B: It drops sharply during the third trimester.
options.D: It decreases by about fifty percent.

explanation: Your kidneys work overtime during pregnancy, filtering blood at a much higher rate to handle waste for both mum and baby. Amazing how the body adapts! [learn more](GNS121_U7_T5#GNS121_U7_T5_h2)

question: At 20 weeks pregnant, a patient's serum creatinine level is 1.0 mg/dL. What does this result suggest?
explanation: Because kidney filtration speeds up during pregnancy, normal creatinine levels actually drop below 1.0 mg/dL. A value of 1.0 mg/dL means the kidneys might not be clearing waste as well as they should right now. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T5#GNS121_U7_T5_h2)

question: How can pregnant women hold onto extra water and sodium without their blood pressure shooting up?

options.A: Renal tubules stop working completely in the second trimester.
options.B: The heart pumps with a much weaker force.
options.C: Excess fluid is immediately stored in the amniotic sac.
options.D: Systemic vascular resistance decreases at the same time.

explanation: Blood vessels relax and widen during pregnancy, giving the extra fluid plenty of room so blood pressure stays nice and stable. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T5#GNS121_U7_T5_h3)

question: How do the kidneys balance out the mild breathing changes (respiratory alkalosis) that happen during pregnancy?

options.A: By excreting more bicarbonate in the urine
options.B: By shutting down the production of red blood cells
options.C: By storing extra carbon dioxide in the renal pelvis
options.D: By absorbing more sodium from the renal tubules

explanation: To keep the body's acid-base balance just right when a mum breathes a bit faster, the kidneys simply let go of some extra bicarbonate in the urine. Brilliant teamwork by the body systems! [learn more](GNS121_U7_T5#GNS121_U7_T5_h3)

question: What is a main reason why women struggle to pass urine during or right after childbirth?

options.A: High concentration of glucose in the urine
options.B: Pressure of the foetal head on the bladder neck
options.C: Sudden complete shutdown of the glomeruli

explanation: As the baby moves down the birth canal, the head can temporarily press on and block the urethra, making it hard to empty the bladder. Totally normal to encounter in labor wards! [learn more](GNS121_U7_T5#GNS121_U7_T5_h4)

question: Why might a woman with an epidural during labor not realize her bladder is getting too full?
explanation: An epidural numbs the lower body nerves, so the normal feeling of needing to pee is blocked. That's why midwives always check and help drain the bladder! Keep this in mind for your clinical postings. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T5#GNS121_U7_T5_h4)

question: What do we call the large amount of urine passed in the first few days after having a baby?
explanation: Postpartum diuresis is just the body's way of getting rid of all that extra pregnancy fluid it doesn't need anymore. Frequent trips to the bathroom are expected! [learn more](GNS121_U7_T5#GNS121_U7_T5_h5)

question: Why are new mums at high risk for their bladders getting overly full right after birth?

options.A: Decreased bladder sensation and birth trauma
options.B: Complete failure of the ureters to drain urine
options.C: High levels of circulating oxytocin in the blood
options.D: A sudden permanent drop in glomerular filtration

explanation: Swelling around the birth area and lingering numbness can trick the bladder, making it hard to empty fully. Good nursing care means keeping a close eye on this! [learn more](GNS121_U7_T5#GNS121_U7_T5_h5)

question: Four hours after a normal vaginal delivery, a mum hasn't peed yet, and her uterus feels soft (boggy) and pushed to the right. What is likely happening?

options.A: Sudden kidney failure caused by blood loss
options.B: A full bladder preventing the uterus from contracting
options.C: Normal postpartum diuresis filling the renal pelvis
options.D: Severe dehydration leading to low urine production

explanation: A full bladder acts like a roadblock, pushing the uterus out of place and stopping it from contracting properly. Always check the bladder if you notice a boggy uterus—it can prevent postpartum hemorrhage! [learn more](GNS121_U7_T5#GNS121_U7_T5_h6)

question: Why do midwives test pregnant women's urine with a dipstick for protein at every antenatal visit?

options.A: To help screen for early signs of preeclampsia
options.B: To measure the exact glomerular filtration rate
options.C: To check if the mother is drinking enough water
options.D: To confirm the presence of a normal twin pregnancy

explanation: Protein in the urine combined with high blood pressure is an early warning sign of preeclampsia. Routine dipsticks are a simple, life-saving tool in antenatal care! [learn more](GNS121_U7_T5#GNS121_U7_T5_h6)
